message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are applied to incoming CSV data or command-line arguments beyond argparse defaults.

No detected untrusted source handling: Pretrained models are loaded via AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained and AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained with no checksum verification, pinned commits/revisions, or source authentication.

No detected label flipping detection: The code reads CSV data and converts labels to integers but performs no distribution comparison, validation against an expected label set, or label-noise detection before training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: No outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs is performed on the training data at any point in the pipeline.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads pretrained models via AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained and AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained using a user-supplied path/name with no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision.

No detected label distribution validation: The code loads datasets from CSV and proceeds directly to training without any class balance checks, expected-label-set validation, or anomaly detection on training samples.

No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural cleanse, activation analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor/trigger defense present anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses standard HuggingFace Trainer and OpenNMT training without any differential privacy library (Opacus, TF Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.).
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) or any adversarial stress tests are used anywhere in the evaluation code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While a separate test split exists (test.csv loaded via DatasetDict), there is no hashing/signing of evaluation data, no explicit isolation enforcement preventing test data leakage into training, and only a single metric source (seqeval) is used without independent verification.
No detected input sanitization: The inference path reads input directly from CSV files and passes tokens to the classifier/normalizer without any shape, range, or schema validation checks.
No detected output bounds checks: The code saves and returns classifier predictions and normalizer outputs without any probability sanity bounds, NaN guards, or threshold checks on the model outputs.

No detected prompt injection defenses: Although the pipeline uses a transformer-based token classifier (distilbert), there is no input filtering, system-prompt isolation, output content moderation, or jailbreak detection implemented anywhere in the visible inference path.
